projectCategory: DSA Module 3.1: Binary Search & Monotonic Search Space Optimization
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Iterative Binary Search on Sorted Array
projects.description: Binary Search is a logarithmic O(log N) algorithm that finds a target value in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. Initialize `low = 0` and `high = N - 1`. Calculate `mid = low + (high - low) / 2` (preventing integer overflow). If `arr[mid] == target`, return `mid`; if `arr[mid] < target`, discard the left half (`low = mid + 1`); else discard the right half (`high = mid - 1`). In this project, you will build an Iterative Binary Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Logarithmic O(log N) Time Complexity, Mid Calculation Overflow Safety & Search Interval Reduction
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Iterative Binary Search ---
Target 40 found at index = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Interval Halving**: Compute `mid = low + (high - low) / 2`.
2. **Comparisons**: If `arr[mid] == target`, return `mid`. Adjust `low` or `high` based on inequality.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `binary_search()`: Performs iterative logarithmic binary search on sorted array.

projects.title: Recursive Binary Search Engine
projects.description: While iterative binary search uses explicit loops, binary search can also be expressed recursively using Divide-and-Conquer. The base case checks if `low > high` (target missing). In the recursive step, compute `mid` and recurse on `[mid + 1 .. high]` or `[low .. mid - 1]`. In this project, you will construct a Recursive Binary Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Divide-and-Conquer Recursion, Call Stack Depth O(log N) & Base Case Handling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Recursive Binary Search ---
Target 23 found at index = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Base Case**: If `low > high`, return -1.
2. **Recursive Decomposition**: Recurse on left or right sub-range.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `binary_search_recursive()`: Performs binary search via call stack recursion.

projects.title: Lower Bound Finder (First Occurrence Index)
projects.description: When duplicate elements exist in a sorted array, standard binary search returns an arbitrary matching index. The Lower Bound algorithm finds the FIRST occurrence index (or smallest index `i` where `arr[i] >= target`). In this project, you will build a Lower Bound Finder in C in O(log N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Lower Bound Mechanics, Duplicate Value Index Bounds & Boundary Preservation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lower Bound Finder (First Occurrence) ---
First occurrence of 4 at index = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Condition**: When `arr[mid] >= target`, record `ans = mid` and move left (`high = mid - 1`).
2. **First Occurrence**: Guarantees finding the earliest duplicate index.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lower_bound()`: Computes lower bound index in sorted array.

projects.title: Upper Bound Finder (Last Occurrence Index)
projects.description: The Upper Bound algorithm finds the first index `i` where `arr[i] > target` (the position immediately following the last occurrence of `target`). Subtracting 1 from upper bound yields the LAST occurrence index. In this project, you will build an Upper Bound Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Upper Bound Mechanics, Range Limit Indexing & Duplicate Element Boundaries
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Upper Bound Finder ---
Upper bound index of 4 is index = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Condition**: When `arr[mid] > target`, record `ans = mid` and move left (`high = mid - 1`).
2. **Right Boundary**: Finds strictly greater index boundary.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `upper_bound()`: Computes upper bound index in sorted array.

projects.title: Count Occurrences of Key in Sorted Array
projects.description: Given a sorted array containing duplicate keys, count the total frequency of a target key in O(log N) time. Using `Count = UpperBound(key) - LowerBound(key)` eliminates linear scanning. In this project, you will build a Sorted Key Frequency Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Range Boundary Subtraction, O(log N) Frequency Counting & Binary Bound Composition
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Occurrences in Sorted Array ---
Total count of key 4 = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Binary Search**: Find `first_idx` and `last_idx` using binary search.
2. **Count Formula**: `count = last_idx - first_idx + 1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_occurrences()`: Calculates key frequency in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Search Insert Position (C++ std::lower_bound Simulator)
projects.description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index if target is found. If not found, return the index where it WOULD be inserted to maintain sorted order (simulating C++ `std::lower_bound`). In this project, you will build a Search Insert Position Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Insertion Index Tracking, Sorted Order Invariant & Boundary Return Logic
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Search Insert Position ---
Insert position for 2 in [1, 3, 5, 6] = 1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Standard Search**: If `arr[mid] == target`, return `mid`.
2. **Insert Point**: When loop terminates `low > high`, `low` holds exact insert position.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `search_insert_position()`: Computes insertion index for sorted arrays.

projects.title: Square Root Integer Computation (sqrt(X)) via Binary Search
projects.description: Compute the floor integer square root `floor(sqrt(X))` without calling `<math.h>` functions. The search space is monotonic: `[1 .. X]`. Compute `mid * mid`: if `mid * mid <= X`, record `ans = mid` and move right (`low = mid + 1`); else move left (`high = mid - 1`). In this project, you will build an Integer Square Root Engine in C in O(log X) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Function Search Spaces, Mathematical Inverse Operations & Long Overflow Handling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Integer Square Root via Binary Search ---
Floor Square Root of 28 = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Monotonic Domain**: `f(mid) = mid * mid` is strictly increasing.
2. **Range Shrink**: Binary search domain `[1 .. X]` in O(log X) time.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `integer_sqrt()`: Computes floor square root using binary search on search space.

projects.title: Find Peak Element in a Unimodal Array (Mountain Array)
projects.description: A peak element is an element strictly greater than its neighbors (`arr[i] > arr[i-1] && arr[i] > arr[i+1]`). In a Mountain Array, elements increase to a single peak and then decrease. Binary search finds the peak index in O(log N) time: if `arr[mid] < arr[mid + 1]`, peak lies on the right slope (`low = mid + 1`); else peak lies on the left slope (`high = mid`). In this project, you will build a Peak Element Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Slope Gradient Binary Search, Unimodal Function Peak Locating & Neighbor Comparisons
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Peak Element in Mountain Array ---
Peak Element = 3 at Index = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Gradient Check**: Compare `arr[mid]` with `arr[mid + 1]`.
2. **Slope Branching**: Upward slope implies peak is to the right; downward slope implies peak is at `mid` or to the left.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_peak_element()`: Locates mountain array peak in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Search in a Rotated Sorted Array
projects.description: Suppose a sorted array is rotated at an unknown pivot index (e.g., `[4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2]`). How do you search for a target in O(log N) time? At least ONE half (`[low..mid]` or `[mid..high]`) is ALWAYS sorted! Check which half is sorted and determine if target falls inside that sorted range. In this project, you will build a Rotated Array Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Rotated Sorted Array Properties, Sorted Half Identification & Range Containment Checks
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Search in Rotated Sorted Array ---
Target 0 found at index = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sorted Half Detection**: If `arr[low] <= arr[mid]`, left half is sorted; else right half is sorted.
2. **Range Test**: Check if target lies within sorted half bounds.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `search_rotated()`: Performs O(log N) binary search on rotated sorted array.

projects.title: Find Minimum Element in a Rotated Sorted Array
projects.description: Find the minimum element (the pivot point) in a rotated sorted array in O(log N) time. If `arr[mid] > arr[high]`, the pivot MUST lie in the right sub-array (`low = mid + 1`); else the pivot lies in the left sub-array (`high = mid`). In this project, you will build a Rotated Minimum Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Pivot Point Extraction, Monotonic Property Breaks & Boundary Min Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Element in Rotated Sorted Array ---
Minimum Element = 1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Compare Mid & High**: If `arr[mid] > arr[high]`, right side contains pivot drop.
2. **Convergence**: `low == high` lands on minimum element.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_min_rotated()`: Finds minimum element in rotated array in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Koko Eating Bananas (Min Speed S to Eat Bananas in H Hours)
projects.description: Koko loves eating bananas from N piles. She has H hours. Find the minimum integer eating speed S (bananas/hr) such that she eats all bananas within H hours. The search space for speed S is `[1 .. max(piles)]`, which is monotonic: if speed S works, any speed > S also works! Binary search on speed S in O(N log(MaxP)) time. In this project, you will build the Koko Eating Bananas Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binary Search on Answer Space, Feasibility Check Functions (`can_eat_all`) & Monotonic Predicates
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Koko Eating Bananas Search Space Optimization ---
Minimum Eating Speed = 4 bananas/hr
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Search Domain**: Speed S range `[1 .. max_pile]`.
2. **Predicate Check**: Calculate total hours required for speed `mid`. If `hours <= H`, try lower speed (`high = mid - 1`).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_eating_speed()` & `can_eat_all()`: Binary search on eating speed answer space.

projects.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
projects.description: A conveyor belt has packages with weights that must be shipped within D days. Find the minimum ship capacity C required. Search space for capacity C is `[max(weights) .. sum(weights)]`. Perform binary search on capacity C in O(N log(SumWeight)) time. In this project, you will build a Ship Capacity Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Capacity Search Space Bounding, Days Feasibility Checks & Monotonic Load Partitioning
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days ---
Minimum Ship Capacity = 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Range Bounds**: `low = max(weights)`, `high = sum(weights)`.
2. **Day Simulation**: Count days needed for candidate capacity `mid`. If `days <= D`, try smaller capacity.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ship_within_days()`: Optimizes ship capacity via binary search.

projects.title: Aggressive Cows / Book Allocation (Maximize Minimum Distance)
projects.description: Given N stall positions and C cows, place all C cows into stalls such that the MINIMUM distance between any two cows is MAXIMIZED. The search space for distance D is `[1 .. max_stall - min_stall]`. Binary search on distance D: if placing C cows with minimum gap D is possible, try larger gap (`low = mid + 1`). In this project, you will build an Aggressive Cows Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Minimax Search Problems, Greedy Placement Predicates & Maximizing Minimum Distance
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Aggressive Cows Maximize Minimum Distance ---
Maximized Minimum Distance = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Greedy Placement**: Place first cow at stall 0. Next cow at first stall >= `last_pos + D`.
2. **Binary Search**: Search distance gap D to maximize minimum separation.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `aggressive_cows()`: Maximizes minimum distance using binary search.

projects.title: Split Array Largest Sum (Minimizing Maximum Subarray Sum)
projects.description: Given an integer array and integer K, split the array into K non-empty contiguous subarrays such that the LARGEST sum among these K subarrays is MINIMIZED. Binary search on candidate maximum sum in `[max_element .. sum_array]`. In this project, you will build a Split Array Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Contiguous Subarray Partitioning, Minimax Sum Search & Monotonic Predicates
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Split Array Largest Sum ---
Minimized Largest Subarray Sum = 18
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Range**: `low = max(nums)`, `high = sum(nums)`.
2. **Greedy Subarrays**: Count subarrays needed if maximum sum limit is `mid`. If `subarrays <= K`, reduce sum limit.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `split_array()`: Minimizes largest subarray sum using binary search.

projects.title: Find Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
projects.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and integer `threshold`, find the smallest divisor D such that the sum of division results `ceil(nums[i] / D)` is <= threshold. Binary search on divisor D in `[1 .. max(nums)]`. In this project, you will build a Smallest Divisor Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Ceiling Division Rules, Divisor Threshold Optimization & Monotonic Search Domain
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold ---
Smallest Divisor = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sum Function**: Compute `sum = sum(ceil(nums[i] / mid))`.
2. **Binary Range**: If `sum <= threshold`, try smaller divisor (`high = mid - 1`).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `smallest_divisor()`: Finds smallest divisor satisfying threshold.

projects.title: Search a 2D Matrix (Row-Major Flattened Binary Search)
projects.description: Given an `R x C` 2D matrix where each row is sorted and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row, search for a target in O(log(R*C)) time. Treat the 2D matrix as a virtual 1D array of size `R*C` where index `i` maps to `matrix[i / C][i % C]`. In this project, you will build a Flattened 2D Matrix Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D to 1D Index Mapping (`row = i / C`, `col = i % C`), Virtual Array Flattening & O(log(R*C)) Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Search a 2D Matrix (Flattened 1D Binary Search) ---
Target 3 FOUND in 2D Matrix!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Virtual Indexing**: Mid index `mid` maps to `(mid / C, mid % C)` in 2D array.
2. **Standard Search**: Run binary search on `[0 .. R*C - 1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `search_matrix()`: Searches 2D matrix via virtual 1D binary search.

projects.title: Search a 2D Matrix II (Staircase Search in Row/Col Sorted Matrix)
projects.description: Given an `R x C` matrix where integers in each row AND each column are sorted in ascending order from left-to-right and top-to-bottom, search for a target in O(R + C) time. Start at top-right corner `(0, C-1)`: if `val == target`, found; if `val > target`, move left (`col--`); if `val < target`, move down (`row++`). In this project, you will build a Staircase Matrix Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Staircase Search Strategy, Top-Right Corner Pivoting & O(R + C) Elimination
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Search a 2D Matrix II (Staircase Search) ---
Target 5 FOUND in Staircase Matrix Search!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Top-Right Pivot**: Top-right cell is max of row 0 and min of col C-1.
2. **Branching**: Decrement `col` if cell too large; increment `row` if cell too small.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `search_staircase()`: Performs O(R + C) staircase matrix search.

projects.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array (Doubles Pattern Binary Search)
projects.description: Given a sorted array where every element appears exactly twice except for one single element, find the single element in O(log N) time. Before the single element, pairs start at EVEN indices `(even, odd)`; after the single element, pairs start at ODD indices `(odd, even)`. Use index parity during binary search. In this project, you will build a Single Element Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Index Parity Analysis, Double Element Pattern Bounds & O(log N) Single Item Locating
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Single Element in Sorted Array ---
Single Non-Duplicate Element = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Parity Check**: Ensure `mid` is even index.
2. **Pattern Test**: If `nums[mid] == nums[mid + 1]`, single element is to the right (`low = mid + 2`); else to the left.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `single_non_duplicate()`: Locates single element using index parity binary search.

projects.title: Find Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
projects.description: Given an `N x N` matrix where each row and column is sorted, find the K-th smallest element. Binary search on value range `[matrix[0][0] .. matrix[N-1][N-1]]`. Count elements `<= mid` in O(N) time using staircase count. Total time O(N log(Max - Min)). In this project, you will build Kth Smallest Matrix Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Matrix Value Range Binary Search, Staircase Counting & O(N log Range) Selection
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Kth Smallest Element in Sorted Matrix ---
The 8-th Smallest Element = 13
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Value Range**: Search space `low = top_left`, `high = bottom_right`.
2. **Staircase Count**: Count elements `<= mid` in matrix in O(N) steps.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `kth_smallest_matrix()`: Computes Kth smallest element in sorted matrix.

projects.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays of Different Sizes in O(log(min(N,M)))
projects.description: Given two sorted arrays A (size N) and B (size M), find their median in `O(log(min(N, M)))` time complexity using binary search partitioning. Partition array A at index `i1` and array B at index `i2` such that `LeftHalfSize == RightHalfSize` and `max(L1, L2) <= min(R1, R2)`. In this project, you will build the Dual Sorted Array Median Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Array Partition Binary Search, Hard Asymptotic Constraint `O(log(min(N,M)))` & Median Formula
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Median of Two Sorted Arrays O(log(min(N,M))) ---
Median = 2.0
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Partition Formula**: Binary search partition index `i1` on smaller array A.
2. **Cross Check**: Verify `L1 <= R2` and `L2 <= R1` to locate exact median cut.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_median_sorted_arrays()`: Solves median of two sorted arrays in O(log(min(N,M))) time.

projects.title: K-th Smallest Pair Distance Engine
projects.description: Given an integer array, the distance of a pair `(A, B)` is `|A - B|`. Find the K-th smallest distance among all possible pairs. Binary search on distance range `[0 .. max - min]`. Count pairs with distance `<= mid` using two pointers in O(N log N) time. In this project, you will build K-th Smallest Pair Distance Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Pair Distance Search Space, Two-Pointer Pair Counting & Binary Distance Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-th Smallest Pair Distance Engine ---
K-th Smallest Absolute Difference Pair = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sort Array**: Sort array to enable two-pointer pair counting.
2. **Binary Search**: Search distance `D` in `[0 .. max - min]` and count pairs with distance `<= D`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `smallest_pair_distance_demo()`: Computes K-th smallest pair distance.

projects.title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
projects.description: Given N gas station positions along a highway and integer K, add K new gas stations such that the MAXIMUM distance between adjacent gas stations is MINIMIZED. Perform binary search on floating point distance D with precision `1e-6`. In this project, you will build a Gas Station Distance Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Continuous Floating Point Binary Search, Precision Tolerances `1e-6` & Minimax Distance
projects.exampleText: Minimize max distance by adding K stations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station ---
Minimized Maximum Distance = 0.500000
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Floating Search**: Binary search on continuous floating distance `D`.
2. **Stations Needed**: Sum `ceil((stations[i+1] - stations[i]) / D) - 1`. If total stations <= K, decrease distance D.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_max_gas_station_demo()`: Optimizes maximum distance between gas stations.

projects.title: Ternary Search Engine for Unimodal Continuous Real Functions
projects.description: Binary search works on monotonic functions. For Unimodal functions (functions that strictly increase then strictly decrease, like a parabola), Ternary Search divides the interval `[low, high]` into THREE parts using `m1 = low + (high - low)/3` and `m2 = high - (high - low)/3` to locate the peak in O(log_1.5 N) time. In this project, you will build a Ternary Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Unimodal Peak Minimization/Maximization, Ternary Search Interval Tri-partitioning & Real Functions
projects.exampleText: Find maximum of parabolic function f(x) on [0, 10]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Ternary Search on Unimodal Real Functions ---
Maximum point located at X = 3.000000
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Tri-partition**: Evaluate `f(m1)` and `f(m2)`.
2. **Narrow Interval**: If `f(m1) < f(m2)`, discard left third `[low .. m1]`; else discard right third `[m2 .. high]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ternary_search()`: Finds maximum point of unimodal real function via ternary search.

projects.title: Fractional Binary Search (Newton-Raphson Style High-Precision Floating Search)
projects.description: Compute high-precision floating point roots `sqrt(2.0)` to 7 decimal places using binary search on floating point domains with termination condition `(high - low > 1e-7)`. In this project, you will build a Fractional Binary Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: High-Precision Floating Binary Search, Epsilon Termination Thresholds (`1e-7`) & Real Roots
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fractional High-Precision Floating Binary Search ---
High-Precision Sqrt(2.0) = 1.4142136
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Epsilon Loop**: Loop while `high - low > 1e-7`.
2. **Float Mid**: Compute `mid = low + (high - low) / 2.0` without integer truncation.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sqrt_float()`: Computes high-precision square root via fractional binary search.

projects.title: Parallel Lock-Free Binary Search Space Partitioning for Massive Data
projects.description: For petabyte-scale search spaces (e.g. GPU database index lookups), partition the search space into independent intervals `[low_i .. high_i]` and run parallel binary searches across worker threads without synchronization locks. In this project, you will build a Parallel Binary Search Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Parallel Search Space Partitioning, GPU Search Acceleration & Lock-Free Thread Independence
projects.exampleText: Parallel search across 8 GPU worker threads
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel Lock-Free Binary Search Space Partitioning ---
Partitioned search space across 8 GPU worker threads simultaneously.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Domain Partition**: Split master domain into N independent sub-ranges.
2. **Parallel Binary Search**: Run binary search on each worker thread concurrently.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `parallel_binary_search_demo()`: Simulates parallel lock-free binary search space partitioning.
